decision: Keep lease authority enforced by coordinator-side expiry and fencing, add an explicit event-loop-starvation regression now, and require cooperative/non-blocking executors for Slice 1. Evaluate an isolated heartbeat supervisor only if real workloads require synchronous CPU-bound execution.
problem: Automatic heartbeat timers run on the worker event loop. A synchronous CPU-bound executor can starve the timer past lease expiry. The worker must never commit a result after authority expires, and another worker must be able to reclaim the mission.

reviews.correctness: Preferred proving the existing coordinator lease-expiry/fencing boundary under deliberate event-loop starvation before adding a second heartbeat authority. A stale worker must fail to complete/fail with its expired lease, and a fresh worker must reclaim and complete.
reviews.robustness_security: Preferred fail-closed stale completion rejection over extending leases or silently accepting late work. Coordinator-side fencing remains authoritative even when the worker runtime cannot schedule its heartbeat timer.
reviews.latency_resources_regression: Preferred a regression test plus cooperative executor contract for Slice 1. A worker-thread/process heartbeat supervisor would preserve liveness for blocking executors but adds IPC, lifecycle, shutdown, crash-reconciliation and resource overhead; defer it until a measured workload demonstrates the need.

alternatives_rejected: Increase lease duration to tolerate CPU blocking: masks starvation, increases stale-owner recovery latency, and does not establish a correctness bound.
Silently clamp heartbeat/lease timing: hides invalid execution assumptions and weakens operator visibility.
Immediately add a heartbeat supervisor thread/process: stronger liveness for blocking executors but materially larger IPC/lifecycle/regression surface before Slice 1 has executable green QA.
qa: Block the worker event loop longer than leaseMs while automatic heartbeat is configured safely.
Assert the starved worker cannot durably complete its stale result.
Assert stale failure persistence is also fenced when authority has expired.
Open a replacement worker on the same durable store, reclaim the mission, and complete it successfully.
failure_lessons: A valid heartbeat interval does not guarantee heartbeat liveness when user execution blocks the event loop.
Lease correctness must be enforced at the durable coordinator boundary, not trusted to worker timers.
Heartbeat supervision is a liveness optimization, not the authority boundary; adding it should not weaken fencing.
remaining_risks: Synchronous CPU-bound executors lose their lease and may waste work; Slice 1 should treat such executors as unsupported until isolated supervision is justified by measurements.
The new regression still requires executable CI evidence before Slice 1 can be frozen.
